items.title: Bill Mays interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 5, 2025
items.q: I read the books on “Canon” and the orchestration books, Mancini’s on the basics of harp writing.

ctx.x: Yeah, and I wrote for two of their albums and it was interesting, I didn’t know a lot about writing for harp at the time. This was maybe 15, 20 years ago when we did these records. And so I read the books on “Canon” and the orchestration books, Mancini’s on the basics of harp writing. And then I wrote some passages and took them to a couple of harp players that I was doing studio work with in New York and said, “Would you play this and tell me what’s wrong or what’s right” and blah-blah-blah. And that’s how I…

able to use the harp in a variety of ways. There’s a bossa nova on one of those records where she’s playing a guitar-like bossa, full chord figures. And the main thing that I needed to learn in that regard was pedal changes and writing chromatically and how to notate it. But there again it brings back the point we made earlier about the necessity is the mother of invention. I had to learn and learn quick what would work and what wouldn’t on the harp. That was a great trio and they were lucky enough to get Heidi…
